title: The Blind Archer
text: An old archer sits on a stump with a bow across his knees, milk-white eyes turned to the sky. Around him stand the targets of every challenger he has beaten, each split dead centre. He has never lost, he says, and he would very much like a game.

options.label: The sharpest eye takes him on, eager to beat the unbeaten.

outcomes.text: They beat him by a hair. He laughs and gives them his quiver, as if he had been waiting years for this.
He wins, as he always does, and gives them a lesson anyway, out of kindness or pity.

options.label: The craftiest moves his target when he isn't looking. He cannot see, after all.

outcomes.text: He hits it anyway, dead centre, and turns his white eyes on the cheat, and does not offer a lesson.

options.label: Decline his game, politely. No one beats an archer who needs no eyes.

outcomes.text: He nods. Most people do. "Then a lesson for free," he says, and shows the Leader how he listens for where a thing will be.

options.label: Whoever carries a bow shoots against him, and puts their own aim to the test.

outcomes.text: They lose, as everyone does, but by so little that he restrings their bow with his own string.
They lose by a mile. He laughs, and shows them why.
